2026-10-17.q: Which statement best captures the main point?
opts: The Government has refused to talk to the unions.
More than 300,000 workers will strike next Wednesday.
The public sector pay dispute has been settled with a new agreement.
A planned strike has been paused while a small team prepares the ground for formal pay talks, but it could still go ahead.
2026-10-17.exp: The strike is "suspended rather than cancelled" and depends on the preliminary talks. No deal exists yet (C), the strike is off for now (B), and talks are starting (A).

2026-10-17.q: What does the passage suggest about the days of confidential contact before the decision?
opts: The unions wanted the strike to go ahead.
The WRC had been abolished.
Both sides were keen to avoid a long conflict.
The Government had already agreed to all pay demands.
2026-10-17.exp: The writer says this contact "indicates a mutual reluctance to prolong the conflict".

2026-10-17.q: The tone of the final paragraph is best described as:
opts: cautious
indifferent
sarcastic
triumphant
2026-10-17.exp: "It should be emphasised that the strike has been suspended rather than cancelled" and its future is "contingent" on the talks — a careful, cautious warning against assuming the dispute is over.

2026-10-17-2.q: What is the passage mainly about?
opts: The planned sale of Ireland's biggest GP network to a US healthcare group, and what it means for patients.
A new law that bans foreign companies from owning GP practices.
The closure of GP practices in the Netherlands and Germany.
Problems with Bon Secours hospitals in Ireland.
2026-10-17-2.exp: The passage reports the agreed acquisition, the buyer, Centric's size, the approval still needed and the reassurance to patients.

Because patients must vote on it.
Because it still needs approval from the competition regulator and others.
Because Dr Maurice Cox has resigned.
2026-10-17-2.exp: "The acquisition is contingent upon approval from the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission and other relevant regulators." The price is undisclosed, not unagreed (A).

2026-10-17-2.q: What is the main purpose of the final paragraph?
opts: To explain Centric's history.
To criticise the new owners.
To reassure patients that their care will continue as before.
To announce new fees for patients.

2026-10-17-3.q: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
opts: Farmers are paid to plough food back into the soil.
Ireland has solved its food waste problem.
Supermarkets in Ireland are being fined for wasting food.
A new Government-backed declaration aims to get more surplus food shared instead of wasted, as a charity says far more could be saved.
2026-10-17-3.exp: The passage centres on the declaration launched at the summit and FoodCloud's argument that much more surplus could be redistributed.

2026-10-17-3.q: Why do farmers sometimes return produce to the soil?
opts: Because charities refuse to accept vegetables.
Because it does not meet buyers' rules on size and shape, or exceeds what their contracts need, and they have no other outlet.
Because the Government requires it.
Because it is not safe to eat.
2026-10-17-3.exp: Surplus arises when farmers "produce more than their contracts require" or produce "fails to satisfy buyers' specifications regarding size and shape"; in such cases they often have "no alternative".

2026-10-17-3.q: Why does the writer mention that saving 3 per cent of surplus could provide 50 million meals?
opts: To show how large the benefit of even a small improvement could be.
To criticise the size of Irish meals.
To prove that FoodCloud already saves 3 per cent.
To explain the COP31 summit.
2026-10-17-3.exp: A small percentage producing a very large number of meals underlines the potential gain — a persuasive use of a statistic.

2026-10-17-4.q: What is the passage mainly about?
opts: A new opera house opening in Dublin next year.
Irish National Opera buying a former church in Dublin as its first permanent home, and its plans for the building.
Problems with gift shops on Dame Street.
The history of Methodist churches in Ireland.
2026-10-17-4.exp: It covers the purchase, its cost and funding, why INO needs space, and the planned uses. An opera house is only a long-term hope (A).

opts: Because it had no upstairs hall.
Because it is far from the city centre.
Because the price was too high.
Because it is a protected structure, which limits how it can be changed.
2026-10-17-4.exp: "The building ... is a protected structure; consequently, commercial interest was limited." It is near O'Connell Street (B) and sold below the guide price (C).

2026-10-17-4.q: Why does the writer mention that Dublin is one of very few European capitals without an opera house?
opts: To show that opera is not popular in Ireland.
To explain why INO sees this purchase as only a first step towards a bigger goal.
To compare ticket prices.
To criticise other European capitals.
2026-10-17-4.exp: The point supports INO's view of the project as "an initial step towards establishing a dedicated opera house".
